newsitem.title: SPAIN: Caja Madrid not eyeing seat on Telefonica board.
newsitem.headline: Caja Madrid not eyeing seat on Telefonica board.

text.p: Caja Madrid is not aiming for a seat on the board of Telefonica de Espana, in which it has bought a three percent stake, a Caja Madrid spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We haven't tried to do that and (the purchase) wasn't made with that intention. That isn't the reason for the investment," the spokesman told Reuters.
Earlier on Tuesday, the savings bank said it had invested 102 billion pesetas in the last two months buying three percent of Telefonica.

The Caja Madrid stake is midway between Banco Santander's -- with some two percent and without board representation -- and those of Argentaria, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya and La Caixa, each of whom hold five percent and two board members each.
Caja Madrid is the fourth largest financial institution in Spain, with loans of 4.1 trillion pesetas last March, and the second largest savings bank.
Its chairman, Miguel Blesa, has been authorised to invest up to 150.0 billion pesetas in assets generally.
The savings bank said its interest in Telefonica was based on diversification in markets and products, as well as the rise in the number of lines.

It also pointed to strong development in mobile phones, the expansion of international unit TISA in strong-growth areas, the new global alliance with BT -MCI and a strong position within the development of Multimedia projects.
In addition, the group's high cash-flow, strong financial health ratio, the maintenance of operating margins and the gradual reduction of extraordinary debt were financial reasons for the purchase.
